blocks.text: The Manner in which Rasulullaah ﷺ Entered Makkah

Ibn Asaakir has narrated from Waaqidi a narration just like that of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) that Tabraani has narrated above. It also mentions that when Abu Sufyaan left (the presence of Rasulullaah ﷺ), Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Abbaas (RA), "Take him to the point where the valley narrows as the mountain protrudes so that he may witness the armies of Allaah passing by." Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) then left the main road and took Abu Sufyaan to the point where the valley narrowed as the mountain protruded.
When Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) held Abu Sufyaan at this point, Abu Sufyaan protested, "Is this betrayal, O family of Haashim?" Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) replied by saying, "Verily, the people of Nabuwaat never betray. I have brought you here for a reason." Abu Sufyaan said, "Then why did you not do this at the beginning and inform me that you needed to bring me here. This would have put me at ease." Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) replied, "It did not occur to me and that you would look at it this way."
Rasulullaah ﷺ had already arranged the lines of the Sahabah (RA) and each tribe began passing by with their leaders. Each battalion also passed by carrying their flags. The first battalion that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent forward was the Banu Sulaym tribe under the leadership of Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA). They numbered a thousand strong. They bore a small flag carried by Hadhrat Abaas bin Mirdaas (RA) as well as another carried by Hadhrat Khufaaf bin Nudba (RA). The large flag was held high by Hadhrat Hajaaj bin Ilaat (RA). Abu Sufyaan asked, "Who are they?" "That is Khaalid bin Waleed," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). "The youngster?" asked Abu Sufyaan. "Yes," was the response. When Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) drew alongside Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) with Abu Sufyaan at his side, the soldiers cried out, "Allaahu Akbar!" thrice before passing by.
Thereafter Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awaam (RA) passed by leading a battalion of five hundred men comprising of Muhaajireen and many unknown people. They carried a black flag and when Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awaam (RA) passed Abu Sufyaan, he called out "Allaahu Akbar!" thrice. His battalion echoed after him. Abu Sufyaan asked, "Who are they?" "That is Zubayr bin Awaam," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). "Your sister's son?" asked Abu Sufyaan. "Yes," was the reply.
Carrying their flag, Hadhrat Abu Dharr Ghifaari (RA) then passed with three hundred soldiers of the Ghifaar tribe. According to other scholars, it was Hadhrat Imaa bin Rahdah (RA) who carried the flag. They also procalimed "Allaahu Akbar!" thrice as they passed Abu Sufyaan. Abu Sufyaan asked, "Who are they, O Abul Fadhl?" "That is the tribe of Ghifaar," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). "What have I to do with the Ghifaar tribe?" responded Abu Sufyaan.
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.167) has commented on the chain of narrators. Bayhaqi has also narrated the Hadith in detail as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.291).
